name: Preston North End Football Club
notes: Both sets of 2024/25 accounts on Companies House are scanned PDFs with no text layer: the figures were read from the page images, so a script that extracts PDF text will not find the evidence phrases. Revenue is the consolidated turnover of Deepdale PNE Holdings Limited (£20,525k); the football club company alone, The Preston North End Football Club Limited, reports turnover of £18,876k, staff costs £25,670k (wages and salaries £22,418k), operating loss £16,017k, loss before tax £15,981k and loss after tax £11,684k. The group holds land and buildings with a net book value of £30,613k (freehold £4,726k, long leasehold £25,887k), but the accounts reviewed do not say who owns the Deepdale freehold, so stadium_owner is left null. Companies House lists Michael Robert Jelski (75% or more, since 20 September 2023) and Kathryn Revitt (75% or more through control over the trustees of a trust, since 11 October 2021) as PSCs of Deepdale PNE Holdings; Trevor Hemmings ceased as PSC on 20 September 2023. Within the group, Deepdale subscribed £13,411,134 for shares in Preston North End Limited and that company £12,025,013 for shares in the club in 2024/25 (intra-group, not recorded as deals); further club share allotments were filed through August 2026. The club's own site (pne.com) renders in the browser and could not be read, and web search ran out, so founding year, Deepdale capacity, kit supplier, shirt sponsor and chief executive are not filled. Craig Hemmings was chairman during 2024/25; Ian Penrose took over on 13 October 2025 (BBC Sport). A sale process was under way in 2026 (talks confirmed January 2026); no completed transaction was found. No valuation or social-follower count found. The club stays in the Championship for 2026/27 (club site season data).

ownership_summary: Owned by the Hemmings family interests. The Preston North End Football Club Limited is wholly owned by Preston North End Limited, which is wholly owned by Deepdale PNE Holdings Limited; the ultimate controlling party is Wordon Limited (Isle of Man), itself controlled by the trustees of a discretionary trust whose potential beneficiaries are certain members of the family of the late Trevor Hemmings. The owners fund the club through interest-free loans from Grovemoor Limited and share subscriptions. Craig Hemmings, Trevor Hemmings' son, stepped down as chairman in October 2025 but remains owner, and the club has been seeking new investment or a buyer since then.
revenue_evidence: Turnover for the year was £20.5m which was higher than the prior year (2024: £16.9m).
